sense: make someone feel awkward or ashamed

terms.comment: “Strike a blush into someone”. Rubor is the blush and the shame behind it, in that sense not frequent before Augustus (Lewis & Short). Feeling embarrassed is mē pudet (see I’m ashamed).

evidence: Plaut. Truc. 2.2.36; Ter. Ad. 4.5.9; Cic. Fam. 5.12 (Lewis & Short)

terms.comment: Traupman’s word for embarrass; classically to throw into confusion, upset, alarm, so it fits only where someone is put out or flustered.

phrases.latin: Ērubuī mēcastor misera propter clāmōrem tuom.
phrases.english: Goodness, poor me, I went red because of your shouting.

sources: Lewis & Short: rubor · Lewis & Short: erubesco · Lewis & Short: perturbo
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 309.
